name: BMW M635 CSi SC
description:
The BMW M635 CSi represents the pinnacle of BMW's first-generation M-car development, based on the elegant E24 6-Series coupe. Introduced in 1983, the M635 CSi (known as the M6 in North America) was BMW's flagship performance car, combining luxurious grand touring comfort with genuine sports car performance.

At its heart was the legendary M88/3 engine, a 3.5-liter inline-six derived from BMW's motorsport programs. This naturally aspirated masterpiece featured individual throttle bodies, a dry-sump lubrication system, and produced 286 horsepower in European specification. The engine was known for its smooth power delivery, high-revving character, and distinctive intake roar.

This SC (Supercharged) variant represents a professionally tuned evolution of the M635 CSi, featuring a supercharger installation that dramatically increases output to 483 horsepower and 595 Nm of torque. The forced induction system transforms the character of the M88 engine while maintaining its legendary reliability and smoothness. With this substantial power increase, the SC variant is capable of exceeding 300 km/h while retaining the refined grand touring manners that made the M635 CSi special.

The M635 CSi featured a sophisticated chassis with independent suspension at all four corners, ventilated disc brakes, and a limited-slip differential. Its combination of performance, luxury, and everyday usability made it one of the most desirable sports coupes of the 1980s.
